descriptionChirho: Gold settings or filigree mountings used for precious stones in the priestly garments, especially the ephod and breastpiece (Exod 28:11,13,14,25, 39:6,13,16,18). The noun mishbetsot refers to the ornamental framework of interwoven gold wire into which gemstones are set. The three clusters differ only grammatically: construct plural 'settings of,' definite article 'the settings,' and prepositional 'of/from settings of.' Translations are consistent: English 'settings,' Spanish 'engastes,' Hindi खाने/खाँचे (slots/settings), Arabic مَشْبَكَتَيْن/أَطْر (lattice-work/frames), Korean 테들 (frames/settings), Swahili vijalizo/vizingiti (mountings/settings).
